rule: Every numeric threshold in a frozen criterion needs a recorded derivation (a physical measurement or a founder decision). An underived number is a defect: it may exist in the record only as a FLAGGED entry with a pending disposition, never silently. Enforced by tests/unit/test_criteria_provenance.py. STRENGTHENED 2026-11-25 (founder correction, 12:00 CT): every SCORING entry declares a 'quantity' class — engine-resolved (a height, position, gap, angle, settle or contact outcome the physics engine already resolves), input-geometry (a dimension of a built/measured object, which must cite its measurement), agreement-statistic (a fraction over verdicts), or physics-state (a boolean read of engine state, no numeric band). A threshold on an engine-resolved quantity with no derivation is a hard failure, and the FLAGGED queue is CLOSED: it holds exactly the entries the 2026-11-25 postmortem recorded (15 after the ring band's resolution) and may only shrink — by derivation, by conversion to a physics-state read, or by founder ruling. A new underived threshold cannot be admitted by flagging it. AMENDED 2026-11-25 (criteria A+B change, queued behind PR #51): twelve of the fifteen flagged entries were resolved -- five by measurement-derived values (SLOT_SIZE, code.tool_angle, CABLE_CHAN_Z_HALF_M, RING_THICK, JITTER xy), three by conversion to physics-state reads (SETTLE_S, GRASP_DIST_M, code.block_inset), four by founder ruling (FRICTION_MULT_RANGE and SECONDARY_THRESH_M adopted as decided conventions, code.reproduced_frac aligned to the v2 Wilson standard, code.bar_80 struck as superseded). The flagged queue now holds exactly the three gripper-device entries (ATTACH_CLOSEDNESS, RELEASE_CLOSEDNESS, GRIP_MIN_EXCURSION_DEG), whose derivation from the arm-calibration plateau data was commissioned 2026-11-25 and lands as a follow-up change.

entries.name: SETTLE_S
entries.derivation: The fixed settle wait never had a derivation -- it was a registered duration ('physics settles for 1.0 s'), and a fixed wait reads whatever state happens to exist when the clock runs out: mid-transient on slow scenes, long after rest on fast ones. No duration gates a score anymore.

entries.name: JITTER
entries.derivation: xy bound is the p90 of the held-out radial pose-error distribution, measured under the twin-suite v1.1 FK-anchor design (S7 dwell selector, per-task x kind median offset fitted on the even-episode train split, residuals on the odd-episode held-out split): pooled p90 = 8.84 cm -> 0.088 m (n=73). The founder adopted the POOLED value as a single tier (ruling 2026-11-25 13:05 CT): the measured per-tier p90s (high 8.71 cm, n=30; medium 9.02 cm, n=41) coincide and their medians invert (high 5.75 cm vs medium 3.39 cm) -- task, not confidence tier, stratifies the error, so separate tiers are not supported by the data. The residual is pipeline pose minus FK-anchored object position at grasp/place dwells and therefore includes the FK anchor's own error (upper-bound-flavoured). The measurement reproduces Builder 2's printed FIX 4 sigma table to the digit from the archived stage-1d rows before deriving any quantile. YAW COMPONENT: recorded as a FLAGGED NULL (None) -- no yaw-error measurement exists in the record (the pose files' sigma_yaw_deg are PCA axis-stability figures, never validated as error), the former 3/6 deg placeholders are REMOVED, not carried forward, and the sampler draws no yaw jitter until a yaw measurement exists (report section 7 specifies what one would need). LOW tier: no value derivable (n=2 held-out); low-confidence poses are denominator-excluded by the pre-registration, so no tier value is needed.
entries.source: jitter-pose-error-measurement-20261125.md sections 4-7 (validator-sets-20261123); builder2-v11-poses.md FIX 3(d)/FIX 4; DGX validation/builder2_stage1d.json (135 rows); jitter-pose-error-residuals-20261125.csv. Adoption: criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).
entries.disposition: RESOLVED 2026-11-25 by the criteria A+B change (queued behind PR #51): see the derivation and criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).

entries.name: JITTER_SIGMA_XY_M
entries.derivation: Per-axis sigma of the same measured pose-error distribution as param.JITTER: pooled held-out sigma/axis = 4.26 cm (n=73; radial RMS / sqrt(2), the record's convention), from the run that reproduces Builder 2's printed FIX 4 sigma table to the digit. This is the Gaussian sigma build_scenes.make_draws samples xy jitter with, for every body and tier: the measured per-tier sigmas (high 0.046 m, medium 0.039 m) do not stratify, and the pose files' per-pose rubric sigmas it replaces (sigma_xy_cm from the pose-estimation.md budget) were a budget, not a measurement.
entries.source: jitter-pose-error-measurement-20261125.md sections 4 and 6 (validator-sets-20261123); adoption: criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).

entries.name: SLOT_SIZE
entries.derivation: Measured from the episodes (P3, confirmed by an independent second opinion that measured blind): channel length 81.0 mm (recess extent, per-episode range 80.2-81.4 mm, n=10 certified-PASS held-out episodes; the first report's 75-79 mm is the seating length -- definitional, both reject 110 mm decisively) and channel width plateau 28.6 mm (per-episode range 27.0-29.4 mm), adopted as 0.029 m. The channel is not uniform: a waist of ~23 mm (adopted scale) is a local narrowing the rectangular SLOT_SIZE model cannot express -- recorded here so the simplification is explicit. The former (0.110, 0.032) was a LOCAL-CHOICE never sourced from the recordings (v1 verifier finding F-04). The same measurement's depth working figure lands as param.SLOT_DEPTH. The corrected geometry was first built as the versioned Stage T scene set (stageT-tool-geometry-20261124.md: length 81 mm, waist 23 / plateau 29 mm, depth 15 mm); this entry lands it in the frozen parameters.
entries.source: tool-slot-second-opinion-20261124.md sections 5.1-5.2 and 7 (validator-sets-20261123); tool-slot-evidence-20261124.md (first report).
entries.disposition: RESOLVED 2026-11-25 by the criteria A+B change (queued behind PR #51): see the derivation and criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).

entries.name: SLOT_DEPTH
entries.derivation: Measured slot recess depth, working figure 15 mm: the second opinion's front-view protrusion bound gives depth >= ~15 mm at the seated bar's socket section (socket diameter ~15.1 mm with its top at or below the foam surface) and >= ~10 mm along the shaft; honest range 12-20 mm. Replaces the former build value depth = P.TOOL_R (5 mm), which the build comment itself labelled '[ESTIMATE, not measured]' -- at least ~3x too shallow at the bar's fat sections. Stage T adopted the same 15 mm in its corrected scene set.
entries.source: tool-slot-second-opinion-20261124.md section 5.3 (validator-sets-20261123); stageT-tool-geometry-20261124.md.

entries.name: SECONDARY_THRESH_M
entries.derivation: Founder ruling 2026-11-25 13:07 CT: the near-miss thresholds (3.0 cm block/eye/tool, 2.0 cm ring, cable exempt) are kept as his DECIDED CONVENTION. The secondary tier is a reporting label on results, not a claim about the world and not the pass/fail criterion; every battery result recorded so far uses these values, and continuity of the record is the point of keeping them.
entries.source: criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat); original registration: twin-replay/twin-replay-preregistration-20261122.md (secondary criterion).
entries.disposition: RESOLVED 2026-11-25 by the criteria A+B change (queued behind PR #51): see the derivation and criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).

entries.name: RING_THICK
entries.derivation: The built ring's tube diameter, measured: the real ring's tube is 11.5 mm in diameter (the value the corrected arm/simulation work uses as 'baseline, real'), adopted into the canonical criteria record on 2026-11-24. The former 0.012 was the ring's MEASURED axial thickness (a flat-faced washer, axial 12.0 mm) consumed in the tube-diameter role -- a measured number in the wrong role (independent critique flag P1, 2026-11-24, upheld the same day). Post-seat-test (PR #51) RING_THICK's scorer role is the non-gating bottom_above_board_m diagnostic and the ring's built geometry; the capsule tube the builders construct is min((RING_R_OUT - RING_R_IN)/2, RING_THICK/2) = 5.75 mm under either value, so no built geometry changes.
entries.source: ring-thickness-diagnostic-20261124.md (validator-sets-20261123): '11.5 mm (baseline, real)'; ring-peg-evidence-20261124.md (measured real parts).
entries.disposition: RESOLVED 2026-11-25 by the criteria A+B change (queued behind PR #51): see the derivation and criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).

entries.name: ring low_ok band [0.0, 0.010] -- REMOVED 2026-11-25
entries.derivation: The band itself never had a derivation -- that was the defect. Its REMOVAL is the founder's recorded decision: the hand-made band approach is rejected, and the seat check is now the physical test (engagement + seat-support contact + settled state) recorded in code.ring_seat_test. The quantity bottom_above_board_m remains in evaluate()'s output as a non-gating diagnostic only.
entries.source: Original defect: lower edge set to exactly 0.0 by the v1.1 fixpass (Builder 1 report: '0 <= ring_bottom - board_top <= 1 cm (v1 credited 5 mm interpenetration)') for textual fidelity to the preregistration; a settled ring reads ~-3 um in the band-edge probe (2026-11-24), so every proven-flat seat failed on this field alone. Removed under: founder ruling 2026-11-25 11:50 CT (zk0 chat) -- replace the band with a physical test: the ring passes only if it is actually engaged on the peg and settled, read from the physics engine's resolved state. Record: twin-replay/ring-band-postmortem-20261125.md.

entries.name: ring seat test = engaged + seat-support contact + settled (physical state; no height band)
entries.pattern: success = bool(engaged and seat_support and settled)
entries.derivation: Founder ruling 2026-11-25 11:50 CT: the seat check reads the physics engine's resolved state instead of a hand-made height band. No chosen numbers: (i) ENGAGED = planar distance within the parts' physical radial clearance RING_R_IN - PEG_R (see code.ring_clearance) AND the ring's vertical extent overlapping the peg's span, both computed from the scene's own geometry (ring hole 22 mm and peg taper ~19.5->15.55 mm measured on the real parts, ring-peg-evidence-20261124.md; modelled peg 16 mm dia. per physics-parameters.md); (ii) SEAT SUPPORT = a contact pair with the board or peg body at settle end -- the same contact-based primary style as the other four tasks; (iii) SETTLED = no active grasp weld on the ring and no arm contact (engine constraint/contact state), and speed below |gravity| x timestep read from the model itself -- one integration step of gravitational velocity gain, the engine's own resolution of 'at rest' (a body in free fall for one step reaches exactly that speed; settled bodies measure orders of magnitude below it). Rim speed converts angular speed with the measured outer radius RING_R_OUT.
entries.source: Founder ruling 2026-11-25 11:50 CT (zk0 chat); recommended disposition in twin-replay/ring-band-postmortem-20261125.md; geometry: twin-replay/physics-parameters.md (Builder A, 2026-11-22), ring-peg-evidence-20261124.md (measured real parts).

entries.name: settle = step until every dynamic object body is at rest (engine rest read; no fixed wait)
entries.derivation: Founder ruling 2026-11-25 (conversion class of the criteria A+B change), replacing the fixed SETTLE_S wait (param.SETTLE_S, removed). _finish steps the scene until every dynamic object body is at rest: linear speed and rim speed (angular speed x the body's bounding radius from the model's own geometry) below one integration step of gravitational velocity gain, |g| * dt, with g and dt read from the model -- the ring seat test's SETTLED clause generalised to every scored body. The step cap is a termination safeguard only: run_episode passes the episode's own trajectory length in steps (a quantity of the episode's data, not a chosen constant), the verdict never reads elapsed settle time, and settle_at_rest in the result records whether rest was actually reached.
entries.source: Founder ruling 2026-11-25; criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat); the settled clause's basis: code.ring_seat_test.

entries.name: grasp attach gate = pad-object contact read (site reaches the object's material; no proximity band)
entries.value: distance-to-material contact read (0 for footprint objects; the object's own radius for axis-measured objects)
entries.derivation: Founder ruling 2026-11-25 (conversion class of the criteria A+B change), replacing the GRASP_DIST_M proximity gate (param.GRASP_DIST_M, removed). Attach at the grasp dwell requires the gripperframe site to reach the object's material: replay.shape_dist() measures planar distance to the material itself for the footprint objects (cube, carton, ring), so contact is 0; for the axis-measured objects (tool, cable segments) it measures to the centreline, so contact is the object's own radius (TOOL_R / CABLE_R, the built geometry). The compact-object centre bound at the snapshot is likewise computed from the object's own footprint extent (cube footprint half-diagonal; ring RING_R_OUT) -- a site in contact is necessarily within it. No chosen tolerance anywhere: contact is the object's geometry, read at the dwell.
entries.source: Founder ruling 2026-11-25; criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat); shape_dist semantics: replay.py run_episode (Builder C, Phase 4, with the changelog #2/#5 dwell-snapshot semantics unchanged).

entries.name: tool axis angle <= 20 deg
entries.derivation: The cap is the measured fixture geometry's own limit: a ~78 mm bar seated in the ~81 mm channel is tilt-capped at ~(81-78)/28.6 ~ 6 deg by the channel end walls, and seated rest angles measured on held-out episodes (9 usable readings, each against the same episode's factory bars) give median -0.5 deg with max |angle| 5.5 deg -- no usable reading exceeds 5.5 deg. The former 20 deg was a registered convention with no derivation; it admitted the 9-19.5 deg leans the critique measured in sim passes, which the real fixture's end walls make impossible.
entries.source: tool-slot-second-opinion-20261124.md section 5.5 (validator-sets-20261123); channel/bar measurements sections 5.1, 5.4.
entries.disposition: RESOLVED 2026-11-25 by the criteria A+B change (queued behind PR #51): see the derivation and criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).

entries.name: block footprint inset factor 0.75 (25%)
entries.derivation: The 25% footprint inset never had a derivation -- it was a registered convention ('center within the lower cube's top footprint (inset by 25%)'), and it fights the physics engine both ways: a cube physically stacked and resting on the lower cube alone fails if its centre overhangs the inset, and a mid-transient contact inside the inset passes with no settled read at all. Its REMOVAL is the founder's 2026-11-25 ruling (the conversion class of the criteria A+B change); the block criterion is now the physical state recorded in code.block_seat_test, and the planar centre offset remains in evaluate()'s output as a diagnostic only.
entries.source: Original: twin-replay/twin-replay-preregistration-20261122.md. Removal: founder ruling 2026-11-25; criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).
entries.disposition: RESOLVED 2026-11-25 by the criteria A+B change (queued behind PR #51): see the derivation and criteria-rulings-20261125.md (validator-sets-20261123); founder rulings 2026-11-25 (zk0 chat).

entries.name: block stack test = contact with lower + sole support + settled (physical state; no footprint band)
entries.pattern: success = bool(contact_lower and no_other_support and settled)
entries.derivation: Founder ruling 2026-11-25 (the conversion class of the criteria A+B change): the block criterion reads the physics engine's resolved state instead of the abolished footprint inset (code.block_inset), mirroring the ring seat test's structure (code.ring_seat_test). No chosen numbers: (i) CONTACT = a contact pair between the upper and lower cubes at settle end; (ii) SUPPORT = the upper cube's contact set is exactly {lower cube} -- the lower cube alone holds it (the pre-existing no-other-support clause, unchanged); (iii) SETTLED = no active grasp weld on the upper cube and no arm contact (engine constraint/contact state), and the upper cube at rest at the engine's own time resolution via replay._body_at_rest (speeds below |gravity| x timestep read from the model; rim speed uses the body's bounding radius from the model's own geometry).
entries.source: Founder ruling 2026-11-25; recommended disposition in twin-replay/ring-band-postmortem-20261125.md.

entries.name: ring engagement = planar <= RING_R_IN - PEG_R (3 mm)
entries.derivation: Physical radial clearance of the modelled parts: the peg cannot pass through the hole beyond RING_R_IN - PEG_R. Computed from measured geometry, not a chosen tolerance (v1's silent +5 mm +2 mm additions were removed by the v1.1 fixpass).

entries.name: evaluate() incidental numerics (indices, rounding, sentinel)

entries.name: episode REPRODUCED iff Wilson lower bound >= 0.6 of valid-variant agreement
entries.derivation: Founder ruling 2026-11-25 13:11 CT: the flat >=60% agreement fraction is replaced by the founder-approved twin-suite v2 standard -- an episode counts as REPRODUCED iff the Wilson score LOWER bound (z=1.96, as in the v2 controls-battery analyzer) of its valid-variant agreement fraction is >= 0.60. One definition of 'counts' across the whole programme: at the registered K=5 variants the flat fraction overclaimed (3/5 agreeing read as reproduced although its Wilson lower bound is ~0.23); the bound is the same 60% the founder approved for v2, now applied at the episode level.
